summary: My best run (0.977896, cell leader at the time) is a5's depth-6/dim-768 shape plus a0's WARMDOWN_RATIO=1.0 plus my own value-embedding placement change {0,1,2,5}; a0's run 6883d9c is the exact control at 0.977973, so my placement change contributed nothing and essentially all of the gain over the 0.997333 baseline came from peers (batch 2**19->2**18, short 256 sliding windows, shallow+wide shape, full-length LR anneal). What did not work, all mine and all now bracketed: removing the tanh logit softcap (+0.0054), tightening it to 8 (+0.0026), value embeddings on all layers (wash), removing value embeddings entirely (+0.0101), and widening the VE input gate from 32 to all residual channels (+0.0009). The one genuinely useful thing my slot produced is the size of the VE effect: value embeddings are worth ~0.010 bpb here, more than the entire batch-size win, yet every knob on them is already at its optimum. What I would try next: the axes my brackets point away from -- continue a5's width curve with the LR retuned for the wider model (dim 896 regressed at inherited LRs, which smells like an LR-vs-width interaction rather than a real width ceiling), and combine a1's Polyak/EMA tail averaging with the full-length anneal, since both target the same end-of-run noise and neither has been measured on top of the other.
